newsitem.title: GERMANY: Flooded E.German farmland put at 15,000 ha.
newsitem.headline: Flooded E.German farmland put at 15,000 ha.

text.p: Some 15,000 hectares of crop and grazing land are submerged after two weeks of flood in the eastern German state of Brandenburg, farm union DBV said in a statement appealing for aid donations.
Citing Brandenburg's DBV branch, the statement said flood-hit farmers needed help with feed and seeds bills and repairs to buildings.
Ground water levels had risen and this was threatening crops in adjacent areas.
On Tuesday, some 7,500 ha were reportedly flooded but heavy rain has further weakened dikes along the German-Polish border.
Thousands of soldiers were laying sandbags to prevent a damaged dike near Hohenwutzen bursting and flooding 250 sq km on Thursday afternoon.
Around 10,000 people of the Oder valley region on Germany's border with Poland were evacuated late on Wednesday after 5,000 evacuations last week.
Livestock evacuations to date include 20,000 beef cattle and 15,000 pigs, which have been put up at farms in other parts of Brandenburg.
DBV said farm minister Jochen Borchert had promised help from the Bonn government and talks with European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler were underway to arrange EU aid.
Land privatisation agency BVVG had decided to waive interest payments on land leases from farmers whose crops had been devastated for one year.
Public sector bank Landwirtschaftliche Rentenbank was offering special conditions on loans to cover damage repairs and reinvestment in houses, machinery and other inputs.
